agree.reason: Starting from her own $600,000 figure and saying early that the tool sits on top of the warehouse system makes a call plausible, but with no cost or payback figure she has little to take to a wary IT director.

honest.reason: The 4.1-to-1.9 figure is correctly called 'more than half' and is credited to one customer, but the subject line turns mis-picks into 'wrong-item returns', and leaving out the second customer's 21% drop makes the result look more typical than it is.

works_the_facts.reason: It quotes the before-and-after rates, but it never works out the 54% cut, never applies it to her $600,000, and never sets 5 sites at $1,250 ($75,000 a year) against the possible savings.

right_comparison.reason: It points to doing nothing through her $600,000 a year, but it never says that cost keeps coming every year or shows what it adds up to if nothing changes.

qualification.reason: One customer's result is presented with no condition attached, such as the range seen across customers (21% to 54%) or a measurable trial target with a date she could check.

objections.reason: It deals directly with the IT director's likely objection ('sits on top', 'doesn't replace it or require re-platforming', three weeks), though it doesn't say how little IT work is involved.

fit.reason: It is short, written as a cold email, easy to read on a phone and ends with a clear request for a call, as the brief asked.
